issues.title: Aggressive URL-based deduplication in VideoDetector loses distinct video elements

sections.body: Navigate to https://www.w3schools.com/html/html5_video.asp and run media.detectVideos
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: 4 results: 2 <video> elements (one with controls, one without) and 4 <source> children
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: 2 results: 1 <video> and 1 <source>. The second <video> and 3 <source> children were lost because they had the same resolvedUrl as the first occurrences.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: VideoDetector.parseResult() at line 104 applies .distinctBy { it.resolvedUrl ?: it.srcUrl } which treats elements with the same media URL as duplicates. Different DOM elements (separate <video> tags, separate <source> children) that happen to reference the same URL are incorrectly collapsed.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/service/VideoDetector.kt:parseResult() line 104
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Use a compound key for deduplication: tagName + resolvedUrl, or include a DOM path/sequence number
- Or remove distinctBy entirely and let consumers deduplicate as needed — the raw detection should report what exists in the DOM
- Add a 'sourceIndex' or 'elementIndex' field to VideoSource so consumers can distinguish multiple elements with the same URL

issues.title: Plugin tools are undocumented in CLI help and invisible to users

sections.body: Run ./b4w.ps1 help or ./b4w.ps1 --help agent and look for media tools
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Plugin tools appear in help output or at minimum there is a hint about how to discover them
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: No mention of plugin tools in help output. Running ./b4w.ps1 plugin (bare) gives error 'Unsupported command form: plugin. Use browser4-cli plugin <subcommand> instead.' No hint to use plugin-media or how to list available tool domains.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The CLI help system only documents built-in commands. Dynamic plugin commands (plugin-<domain>) are discovered at runtime from the server's /mcp/tools endpoint, but this discovery is not surfaced in help output. The bare 'plugin' command is blocked by preferred_spaced_command_form() before reaching the dynamic plugin handler.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs: lines 15080-15090 (preferred_spaced_command_form blocks bare 'plugin') and help generation code
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a 'Plugin Tools' section to the main help output listing available plugin-<domain> commands
- Fix the bare 'plugin' command to work and list available tool domains (it already has the code for this at line 11981-11989 but can't be reached)
- Add a '--help plugins' category filter
- Consider listing plugin tools in the output of ./b4w.ps1 --help agent

issues.title: Complex return types wrapped in description maps lose structured data

sections.body: Call media.download or media.getInfo — observe the response format
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clean JSON with fields like {"success": true, "filePath": "...", "bytesDownloaded": 788493}
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Result wrapped in {"type":"...DownloadResult","description":"DownloadResult(url=..., filePath=..., ...)"} — a toString() representation in a description field. Consumers must parse the description string to extract field values.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: AbstractToolExecutor.callFunctionOn(ToolCall, Any) at line 76-86 wraps non-primitive, non-collection results in a description map to prevent Jackson from walking into internal object graphs. While this prevents serialization errors, it makes the output effectively unparseable for machine consumers.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/builtin/AbstractToolExecutor.kt: lines 76-86
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a marker interface (e.g. SafeToSerialize) that domain result classes can implement to opt into direct JSON serialization
- Or annotate result data classes with Jackson annotations so they serialize cleanly
- As a minimum, include a 'fields' map alongside the description so machines can access individual fields without parsing
